title: The Cell's Tiny Organs
hook: Inside a single cell sits a whole working city — a control room, power plants, factories, and shipping lanes, each a structure called an organelle.
key_points: Organelles are specialized structures inside a cell, each doing a particular job.
The nucleus stores DNA and acts as the cell's control center.
Mitochondria release energy from food; ribosomes build proteins.
The endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus process and ship those proteins.
content_html: A eukaryotic cell isn't an empty bag of fluid — it's packed with tiny structures called organelles, each handling a specific task. Think of it as a miniature city: the nucleus is the control room storing the master plans (DNA), mitochondria are power plants, ribosomes are factories, and a network of membranes ships goods around.
extra_html: Each organelle has a clear role. The nucleus guards the cell's DNA and decides which genes get used. Mitochondria break down food molecules to release usable energy, which is why they're nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell. Ribosomes read genetic instructions and build proteins. Newly made proteins often travel through the endoplasmic reticulum (a folded membrane network) and then the Golgi apparatus, which modifies, packages, and labels them for delivery. Khan Academy's tour of organelles walks through each structure and how they cooperate to keep the cell alive and busy.

related.title: What Is a Cell?
related.hook: Every living thing — from a bacterium to a blue whale — is built from cells, the smallest unit that can call itself alive.

related.title: Two Kinds of Cells
related.hook: All cells fall into two camps: simple prokaryotes with no nucleus, and complex eukaryotes that pack their DNA into a sealed control room.

related.title: The Cell Membrane: Gatekeeper of the Cell
related.hook: A flexible, oily film just two molecules thick decides what enters and leaves every cell — and it pulls off some of that traffic for free.

flashcards.back_html: A specialized structure inside a cell that performs a specific job — like a tiny organ. Examples include the nucleus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.

flashcards.prompt: Which organelle stores the cell's DNA and directs its activities?
flashcards.explanation_html: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and acts as its control center, directing which proteins get made and when.

flashcards.prompt: Where in the cell are proteins assembled?
flashcards.explanation_html: Ribosomes read genetic instructions and string amino acids together into proteins. They float freely or sit on the endoplasmic reticulum.
